            on:

Religions   
            & Beliefs in Ancient Iran

 

				This page curates links to peer reviewed scholarship on 
				religions and beliefs in ancient Iran and the wider Iranian 
				world, with particular attention to religious practice, 
				institutions, and intellectual traditions across time and space. 
				It brings together research on Iranian ritual and cult, sacred 
				landscapes and temple economies, priestly authority and legal 
				norms, and the circulation of religious knowledge, alongside 
				studies grounded in archaeology and material culture, 
				iconography, epigraphic and numismatic evidence, and 
				philological analysis of Avestan, Old Persian, Middle Persian, 
				and related corpora. The collection also engages critically with 
				scholarship on Zoroastrianism in its historical plurality, as 
				well as on interreligious contact and competition, including 
				encounters with Mesopotamian and other traditions. Throughout, 
				it foregrounds methodological rigour, directing readers to work 
				that scrutinises source conditions, transmission histories, 
				interpretative frameworks, and evidential limits, including 
				debates over periodisation, the relationship between doctrine 
				and practice, and the political uses of religious narratives and 
				categories.
